Let's carefully examine what perigee values appear on the Moon Wikipedia page! In the infobox: `| periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` Wait! Look at the range in the infobox: `({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` And in text: `The distance between the Moon and Earth varies from around {{convert|356,400|km|mi|abbr=on}} ([[perigee]]) to {{convert|406,700|km|mi|abbr=on}} (apogee)` Wait, another place in text: `ranging from {{convert|357000|-|407000|km|mi|sp=us}}` Wait! What is the "minimum perigee value on the Wikipedia page for the Moon"? Is it 356,400 km or 356400 km or 356 400 km? Wait, let's check all numbers on the Wikipedia page for Moon that represent minimum perigee or periapsis! Let's print the entire infobox of the Moon page!```python cmd = """curl -s -A "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)" "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=content&format=json&titles=Moon" | python3 -c "import sys, json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); wt=list(data['query']['pages'].values())[0]['revisions'][0]['*']; print(wt[:4000])" """ out = await run_command(cmd) print(out) ```
